content:
I am a bit confused about the comment in the following:

  /-- Construct a seminormed group from a seminorm, i.e., registering the pseudodistance
and the pseudometric space structure from the seminorm properties. Note that in most cases this
instance creates bad definitional equalities (e.g., it does not take into account a possibly
existing `UniformSpace` instance on `E`). -/]
abbrev GroupSeminorm.toSeminormedGroup [Group E] (f : GroupSeminorm E) : SeminormedGroup E where

Is this saying that if I want to create an instance of a SeminormedGroup I should never use this and instead create the usual structure via PseudoMetricSpace?
Or is it okay to use this in general when the group does not have any UniformSpace instances?
It's ok to use this if your group has no existing UniformSpace or TopologicalSpace or PseudoMetricSpace instances
